_meta.description: Policy the two agents run on. RoutingAgent: matches tasks to contributors, queues on capacity, recovers from decline/failure. TrackingAgent: owns the quality of estimate and status data that RoutingAgent's capacity and queueing decisions depend on. Everything here is data so the operator can tune it without code changes.

RoutingAgent.owns: routing requests, eligibility, capacity checks, queueing, recovery proposals
RoutingAgent.reads_from_tracking: confirmed estimates, hours_remaining, plan_health, estimate debt

TrackingAgent.also_runs: periodic sweep over every active assignment (default every 60 simulated seconds in a demo, every 15 minutes in real time)
TrackingAgent.owns: estimates, status check-ins, plan health, data-quality alerts
TrackingAgent.contract: Every accepted assignment gets a contributor-confirmed estimate within the SLA for its priority, and stays fresh afterwards. RoutingAgent never trusts an unconfirmed number without marking it as such.

routing.stuck_note: Flag only. A stuck request is never failed automatically; the operator cannot know whether it is slow or lost.

sources.requester_provisional: tasks[].estimated_effort_hours, entered at submission. Treated as a guess.
sources.contributor_confirmed: Entered by the assigned contributor, ideally in the same form that accepts the assignment. Revisable; every revision is kept.
sources.check_in_remaining: hours_remaining from a status check-in. Most current view of what is left.

capacity_precedence: latest estimate revision (contributor_confirmed or check_in; most recent wins)
model.rule: Capacity and conflict checks use the latest estimate revision for the assignment (a check-in is stored as a revision with source=check_in, so the most recent honest number wins), falling back to the requester estimate. Anything derived from requester_provisional is labelled 'unconfirmed' in the conflict warning and the operator question, with the buffer applied.

capture_at_accept.rule: The accept action requires hours_total and confidence. A contributor can only move an assignment to in_progress with a confirmed estimate. Assignments created another way (operator manual assign, simulation) start as awaiting_estimate and are chased by the TrackingAgent.

estimates.sla_note: estimate_due is counted from the moment the assignment is accepted (or manually assigned). Minutes are simulated and compressed by contributor_engagement.status_check.demo_compression_factor.
chase_ladder: t0: assignment accepted or assigned -> TrackingAgent sends an estimate request to the contributor
t0 + estimate_due: no estimate -> plan_health = overdue_estimate, first reminder
every reminder_every: reminder until max_reminders reached
after max_reminders unanswered: raise alert 'estimate_overdue' and operator question 'estimate_missing'

validation_rules.variance_note: Contributor hours_total differs from the requester estimate by more than this percent -> 'estimate_variance' alert + question (the task may be mis-scoped).
validation_rules.remaining_increase_note: hours_remaining rises by more than this percent between revisions -> 'estimate_variance' (scope growth).
validation_rules.remaining_exceeds_time_to_due: hours_remaining > working hours left before due date (elapsed hours x working_hours_per_day / 24) -> 'due_date_at_risk'. Due dates are real time and are NOT compressed by the demo factor.

plan_health_values.complete: Confirmed estimate present, fresh, within validation rules.
plan_health_values.overdue_estimate: Past estimate_due with no confirmed estimate.
plan_health_values.stale: Estimate or status older than stale_after_minutes.
plan_health_values.at_risk: Contributor reported at_risk/blocked, or hours_remaining exceeds time to due.

estimate_debt.rule: A contributor with more than this many assignments in overdue_estimate is treated by RoutingAgent as capacity-unknown: other eligible contributors are preferred; if they are the only option, the task is queued with an 'estimate debt' warning (capacity_conflict reason) instead of being assigned.

daily_report_metrics: estimate_coverage_pct: confirmed estimates within SLA / accepted assignments
capacity decisions made on unconfirmed estimates

alerts.rule: severity = clamp(priority_rank(task.priority) + triggers[trigger].adjust, floor, 4), where floor = 1 (low) if the trigger needs_action, else 0 (info). A decision the operator must make can therefore never be log-only. 'info' alerts are log-only and appear in the daily report.

stuck_request.question: stuck_request
stuck_request.description: Routing request pending longer than the stuck threshold for its priority.

capacity_conflict.question: capacity_conflict
capacity_conflict.description: Every eligible contributor would exceed task-count or hours capacity, or has estimate debt; task queued.

priority_contention.question: priority_contention
priority_contention.description: Two or more queued tasks compete for the same contributor's remaining capacity.

estimate_overdue.question: estimate_missing
estimate_overdue.description: No confirmed estimate after the SLA and all reminders.

estimate_stale.question: estimate_missing
estimate_stale.description: Estimate or status not refreshed within the stale window.

estimate_variance.question: estimate_variance
estimate_variance.description: Contributor estimate differs sharply from the requester's, or remaining hours grew sharply.

estimate_debt.question: estimate_missing
estimate_debt.description: Contributor has more overdue estimates than allowed; RoutingAgent will avoid assigning more.

status_no_response.question: contributor_silent
status_no_response.description: Contributor missed the configured number of status check-ins.

status_at_risk.question: at_risk
status_at_risk.description: Contributor reports the task may miss its due date.

due_date_at_risk.question: at_risk
due_date_at_risk.description: Remaining hours exceed hours left before the due date.

late_return_superseded.description: A routing result arrived after the operator intervened; recorded and ignored.

channel_notes.in_app_banner: Pinned banner + badge in the operator inbox until acknowledged.
channel_notes.in_app: Badge and entry in the operator inbox.
channel_notes.in_app_digest: Grouped into an hourly digest entry, no banner.
channel_notes.outbox: Simulated external delivery (email/chat): written to an outbox table and shown in the UI so the demo needs no real service. Swappable for a real notifier later.
channel_notes.log_only: Event log and daily report only.

alerts.escalation: An unacknowledged alert re-alerts per delivery_by_severity and is raised one severity level on the final re-alert.

principles: The agent asks, the operator decides: no question is ever auto-answered with a state-changing action.
Every question states what the agent knows (task, eligible set, load, elapsed time, estimate source and confidence) and offers explicit options with consequences.
If unanswered by the timeout, the agent applies only the 'safe_default' (never reassign/cancel), re-alerts, and keeps the question open.
Questions and answers are events (who, when, option, free-text note) and persist across restarts.

stuck_request.prompt: Routing for {task} has been pending {elapsed}s with no response. What should I do?

no_match.prompt: No contributor matches {task} (area {area}, min level {min_level}). How do you want to proceed?

capacity_conflict.prompt: {contributor} would be over capacity ({reasons}; load basis: {estimate_basis}) if given {task}. The task is queued. Options?

priority_contention.prompt: {tasks} are competing for {contributor}'s remaining {hours}h. Which goes first?

estimate_missing.prompt: {contributor} has not provided a confirmed estimate for {task} ({issue}: {minutes_overdue} min past the SLA, {reminders} reminders sent). Planning currently uses {fallback_hours}h from {fallback_source}. What now?

estimate_variance.prompt: {contributor} estimates {task} at {contributor_hours}h versus {requester_hours}h from the requester ({delta_pct}%). Which is right?

contributor_silent.prompt: {contributor} has not answered {missed} status check-ins on {task}. How should I proceed?

at_risk.prompt: {task} is {state} ({detail}). Should I change the plan?

status_check.demo_compression_note: Cadences and estimate SLAs are in simulated minutes. A factor of 60 means 1 simulated hour passes per real minute, so check-ins are visible in a demo. Routing latency (5-20s) is NOT compressed.
status_check.effect_on_planning: hours_remaining is the top source in estimates.model.capacity_precedence, so capacity and capacity_conflict checks use the latest honest number.

contributor_engagement.contributor_inbox: Simulated: the UI exposes a contributor view where the demo user can accept with an estimate, respond to estimate requests and respond to check-ins. Seed tasks can script replies with tasks[].sim.estimate and tasks[].sim.status_check.
